description: Hi i am an individual participant.
summary:
Built a complete, closed-loop CubeSat Digital Twin integrating live NASA TLE/SGP4 orbital physics, NASA F Prime (C++17) 1 Hz autonomous FDIR flight software, and NASA Open MCT mission control.

Automated the entire workflow with a one-command bash launcher, live WGS84 coordinate streaming, and post-run engineering plots—running smoothly on standard laptop hardware.
details:
How It Works

Our system closes the loop between space-environment physics, onboard flight software, and ground mission control at a deterministic 1 Hz execution rate:

1. Orbital & Power Physics Plant (Python):

- Fetches real-time International Space Station (ISS) Two-Line Element (TLE) orbital parameters from NASA's public TLE API (with offline fallback).

- Propagates 3D ECI position/velocity vectors using SGP4, computes Earth-shadow eclipse intervals via solar-vector geometry, and converts orbital coordinates into WGS84 sub-satellite latitude and longitude.

- Simulates a CubeSat Electrical Power System (EPS) including solar array generation, bus voltage, battery State of Charge (SoC), payload power draw, and thermal dynamics, supporting time-acceleration (--warp) to compress a 92-minute orbit into ~2 minutes of testing.

2. Flight-Grade Onboard Autonomy (NASA F Prime in C++17):

- A custom PlantBridge component receives 32-byte binary UDP sensor packets from the physics plant at 1 Hz and dispatches them into the F' flight software topology.

- A deterministic 1 Hz RateGroup drives our PowerFdir component, which implements a three-tier autonomous state machine:

NOMINAL (SoC > 45%): Full payload operations in Earth-facing NADIR attitude.

LOAD_SHED (SoC <= 40%): Sheds secondary heaters and cameras while maintaining mission pointing.

SAFE_MODE (SoC <= 20% or Bus Voltage < 6.8 V): Cuts power to survival-only avionics and commands SUN_POINTING attitude to maximize solar recharge.

- Hysteresis logic prevents rapid mode oscillation at threshold boundaries, and PlantBridge transmits 8-byte binary actuator commands back to the physics plant to close the loop.

3. Ground Mission Control & Post-Mission Analytics (NASA Open MCT & Matplotlib):

- Operators monitor 9 live telemetry channels (Battery SoC, Bus Voltage, Solar Current, Temperature, Eclipse State, FDIR Mode, Attitude Mode, Latitude, Longitude) and Flight Event Records (EVRs) in NASA Open MCT, and can uplink manual RESET_SAFE_MODE commands.

- An automated bash launcher (start_sim.sh) orchestrates all processes and generates timestamped CSV telemetry logs, multi-panel power/FDIR summary charts, and dual-hemisphere WGS84 ground-track maps pinpointing where Safe Mode triggers occurred.

Benefits & What We Hope to Achieve

- Interactive Mission Trade-Off Exploration: Allows students, engineers, and mission planners to test how initial battery capacity, eclipse durations, and FDIR thresholds impact spacecraft survival.

- Pre-Flight Software Verification: De-risks embedded flight code, telemetry dictionaries, and ground-control procedures on a standard laptop before Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) or flight testing.

- Accessible Aerospace Engineering: Demonstrates that authentic NASA flight frameworks (F Prime and Open MCT) can be unified into an approachable, open-source simulation sandbox.
